text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The planned Estonian-American joint venture Narva Power presented its business plan to Economy Minister Jaak Leimann Monday. The U.S. side will pay $67.2 million and the plan will be valid from January 1, 1998, if the government approves it.
- The parliamentary opposition made further attempts to amend the law on customs tariffs, but the ruling coalition says that the amendments will not be approved.
- The symphony No 5 by Estonian composer Lepo Sumera came second at the International Rostrum of Composers in Paris.
- The Tallinn central prison management was replaced by the board of prisons.
- The visa-free travel agreement with Finland has increased the number of Finnish tourists by 25 percent compared to last year.

- The Leningrad district has announced that it is not interested in the financing of a planned new bridge between Estonia and Russia due to reduced traffic volume. The new bridge outside Narva and its access roads would cost $100 million.
